findings.summary: craftSlotValue (4337) values a piece at max(sale, dis) gated by sale>need where need=dis+0.10; the 0.10 is never subtracted from pieces that do list. The comment at 4406-4414 says the bar exists because a listing 'costs attention... five copper a listing'. At fee 0.05: 3.6591 (+3.07%); fee 0.20: 3.6022 (+1.47%). verdict.reasoning:

Re-read test60.html:4316-4344: craftSlotValue does `if(!stat||stat.median==null)continue` then `wsum++` only for priced rolls and returns vsum/wsum, so the slot value is the mean over covered rolls only; craftExpected (4346-4357) weights slots by CRAFT_SLOT_WEIGHT/wsum — mechanism as stated. fillQuiet (4496-4513) sets only x.sell / x.from, never a price; the comment above it explicitly says the neighbour price is a lower bound only ~2/3 of the time and 'settles the verdict, never the price'.

Independent script refute-ev3/knife_check.py (`python3 knife_check.py`): knife priced 46/100, all 46 sell, priced mean 1.9175, page slot value 1.8983 (= ev_ref); fill sources 22 wide / 30 nbr / 2 none; wide-filled mean 1.7811, nbr-filled mean 1.7941; fill slot value 1.8306 over 98, 52 sell; case gross 3.6655, +3.25%; scrap-for-unpriced 3.6230, +2.06%. Daily knife median moves 1.77→2.00→1.86 across the week, not monotone, so no drift story. The claim holds, but the sharper mechanism (refute-ev3/corner.txt, knife_bias.py) is that renormalisation overweights the three corner premium rolls 40/5 (4.33), 40/4 (2.85), 39/5 (2.40): they carry 3/46 of the slot instead of 3/100 — 0.2062 vs 0.0948 of slot value, a 0.111 overstatement by itself; the other 43 priced rolls average 1.8285, close to the unpriced population (1.78-1.80). Sample-size caveat: 11 of the 22 wide-filled rolls have a single retained sale, but the 298 7-day sales on unpriced rolls median 1.8045, so the level is not a small-n artefact.

Counterfactual range (knife_bias.py): two-sided interpolation from priced rolls only gives knife 1.8614 → case 3.6712, +3.42%; interpolation from priced+retained 1.8314 → +3.26%; finding's fill 1.8306 → +3.25%; scrap floor +2.06%. claim_verdicts.claim: Claim 4a: the plain median is the best available point estimate of what a roll clears at; no other estimator does materially better
claim_verdicts.reason: Rolling-origin out-of-sample test (8,927 roll-origins, 965 rolls, 245,238 scored next-day sales, b_oos.out): plain 48h median relMAE 2.89%; the best alternatives are the collector's recency-weighted median (2.82%, -0.06 pts, cluster-boot CI [-0.10,-0.03]) and the collector's selected 24h/48h (2.84%, -0.05). Everything else is worse (trim20 +0.04, ret7 +0.07, q75 +0.11, last3 +0.19, rwmean +0.19, plain mean +0.27, q25 +0.47). Same ranking at 6h horizon and in every count bucket. The 0.06-0.11 pt gains are statistically real but ~2-3% relative and move case EV by <=0.12 pts (weighted_median +3.49% vs +3.61%, README). Against the realised next-day median the 48h median is unbiased-to-slightly-low (-0.28% mean, -0.41% median; bias2.out).

claim_verdicts.claim: Claim 4b: the median (not the upper quartile) is the right LISTING price, evidenced by the split test (+0.68% for 6x the wait)
claim_verdicts.reason: The split test reproduces in direction and magnitude (threshold >=7 non-stale sales in 48h: 558 rolls / 43,844 sales; Q3/median-1 = +0.72% median-by-roll, +1.05% mean-by-roll; median time-to-sell 45.2 min at >=Q3 vs 5.9 min at <=median, 7.6x; a_split.out). Caveat: this and any sales-only test cannot establish revenue-optimality, because listings that never sold are invisible (survivorship). The observable proxy: 61.6% of next-day sales clear at/above the median estimate vs 47.9% at Q75 and 74.8% at Q25 (b_oos.out). Also basic tier is the exception where Q3 buys +3.6% for 126 vs 14 min.

claim_verdicts.claim: Claim 6a: a binary count-based thin marker (selected.count < THIN_SALES) is the right thin-evidence signal
claim_verdicts.reason: Out of sample the marker barely discriminates: it flags 30.1% of roll-origins, and only 8.0% of flagged ones have a next-day median >5% off the estimate vs 5.9% base rate; recall 41% (d2_marker.out). Next-day p90 error is flat from n=2 (3.9%) through n=9 (3.7%); only n=1 stands out (7.2%, 14.2% >5%). Tier dominates count: basic p90 12.3% (32.5% of origins >5% off) vs elite 2.6% (1.9%). A dispersion marker (48h IQR/median > 5%) flags 10.1% with 22.4% precision, 2.8x the count marker; bootstrap-CI half-width > 3% flags 10.2% with 23.4%.

claim_verdicts.claim: Claim 6b: 5 is the right cut for the marker
claim_verdicts.reason: Subsample test on 386 rolls with >=30 sales in 48h (d_thin.out): p90 relative error of a subsample median vs full median is 5.5% (n=1), 6.2% (n=2; median of 2 = mean), 2.7% (n=3), 2.6% (n=4), 2.2% (n=5), 1.6% (n=8), 1.4% (n=10). The knee is n=2->3 (-56%); 3->5 removes 0.56 pts, 5->8 another 0.55 pts; nothing singles out 5. Per tier at n=5: basic p90 13.7% vs elite 1.5% - a basic roll with 30 sales is less certain than an elite roll with 2. Changing the cut is low stakes (no EV or sell/break verdict depends on it), which is why it is wrong-but-harmless.

findings.title: Swing line's 'cases before profit reliably beats the swing' uses the edge at the current caseCount, not at the n it recommends: 12,100 shown, >=25,500 at the visible book, fixed point ~28,900
findings.summary: paintCase computes need=(2*sd/edge)^2 with edge=gross-cost.unit where cost=craftWalk('case1',n) for the caseCount in the input (default 1 -> unit 3.55, edge 0.1281 -> 12,100). But 12,100 cases cannot be bought at 3.55: the visible book holds 4,766 cases up to 3.599; walking it (remainder at the 3.599 floor) gives unit 3.58966 at n=12,100, edge 0.0884, need 25,473 -> 25,500; iterating to self-consistency gives n=28,916 (unit 3.59509, edge 0.0830), itself a floor since deeper asks are unseen. The page already shows this drift when the user types n (n=1000: 13,400; n=9999: 24,400) but at the default n=1 the figure understates the requirement by 2.1-2.4x. The formula and wording are otherwise right: MC of 300 batches of 12,100 at unit 3.55 -> P(profit>0)=97.7% = Phi(2), median profit 1,616, p10 544.
